title: OET Reading: Three Parts in 60 Minutes
summary: OET Reading's three parts — fast text-matching, gap-fill from short texts, and two longer passages — and how to beat the clock.

chunks.heading: Three parts, 60 minutes, healthcare texts
chunks.body: OET Reading has **three parts, about 42 questions in 60 minutes**, on **generic healthcare topics**. Part A is **strictly timed (~15 minutes)** and speed-based; Parts B and C give you the remaining time for shorter and longer texts.
chunks.realExample: Because Part A has its own tight time limit, treat it as a separate sprint — don't carry a slow Part A pace into it or you'll run out before finishing.
chunks.memoryHook: 3 parts, 60 min total. Part A is a ~15-min sprint; B & C take the rest.

chunks.heading: Part A — scan four texts fast
chunks.body: Part A gives **four short healthcare texts** and questions (matching, sentence completion, short answer) that you answer by **quickly locating information across the texts**. It's a **skimming-and-scanning** race — find the right text and spot, don't read everything.
chunks.realExample: A question asks which text mentions a dosage — scan headings and keywords to jump to the right text, grab the figure, and move on. Speed and location, not deep reading.
chunks.memoryHook: Part A = locate fast across 4 texts. Scan for the keyword; don't read it all.

chunks.heading: Parts B & C — read for meaning
chunks.body: **Part B** has **short workplace texts** (memos, guidelines, notices) with one multiple-choice question each — catch the **main point or detail**. **Part C** has **two longer passages** testing **deeper comprehension, opinion and attitude**, so read those more carefully.
chunks.realExample: A Part B guideline extract may hinge on one instruction ('administer only if…'); a Part C opinion piece may ask the writer's stance — match the reading depth to the part.
chunks.memoryHook: B = quick point per short text. C = deeper meaning in two longer passages.

chunks.heading: Manage the clock across parts
chunks.body: Because Part A is separately timed, **finish Parts B and C without overspending** on any one question. Answer what's clear first, flag the tricky ones, and **never leave a blank** — there's no penalty for wrong answers.
chunks.realExample: Stuck on a Part C inference? Mark it, keep answering, and return with spare time — a guessed answer can score, a blank never will.
chunks.memoryHook: Budget across B & C, flag the hard ones, guess before the end. No blanks.

recall.a: Three parts with about 42 questions in 60 minutes, on generic healthcare topics.
It's strictly timed (about 15 minutes) and speed-based — you scan four short texts to locate information fast.

recall.q: How do Parts B and C differ?
recall.a: Part B has short workplace texts with one question each (main point/detail); Part C has two longer passages testing deeper comprehension, opinion and attitude.

recall.q: What reading technique wins Part A?
recall.a: Skimming and scanning to find the right text and spot quickly, rather than reading everything.

recall.q: Should you leave OET Reading questions blank?
recall.a: No — there's no penalty, so flag hard ones and guess before time runs out.
